newsitem.title: FRANCE: Missing French aid workers held in Chechnya - group.
newsitem.headline: Missing French aid workers held in Chechnya - group.

text.p: Four Frenchmen missing in Russia's Dagestan republic in the north Caucasus are being held in neighbouring Chechnya, where they are in good health and well treated, their refugee relief group said on Monday.
Rene Kergall, director general of the relief organisation Equilibre, told Reuters he believed the kidnapping was "a case of banditry" and not politically motivated.
The Russian Foreign Ministry provided the first official confirmation of their fate to Equilibre's office in Makhachkala, the capital of Dagestan, he said.
The four disappeared on August 3, the latest in a string of foreign relief workers kidnapped for ransom in and around Chechnya in recent months.
"I am very pleased that they have been found," Kergall said, adding that negotiations for their release were continuing.
The four men had been in Dagestan, a small republic in the extreme southeastern corner of the Russian Federation, for several months to aid refugees from Chechnya.
